title: Graded Health Adapter for Request Prioritization and Autoscaler Stabilization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current binary readiness/liveness probes cause brittle autoscaler behavior during transient overloads and multi-region failovers. Services flip between Ready/NotReady and trigger thrashing autoscaling events or aggressive load-shedding that violates tail SLOs for high-priority clients.

Goal: Implement a "graded health adapter" that converts a stream of telemetry (latency percentiles, queue depth, token budgets, memory pressure, recent error-rate) into a continuous health score (0.0-1.0). Use that score for:
- admission control (request prioritization and soft-deny thresholds),
- autoscaler hysteresis tuning (smoother scale decisions),
- multi-region failover weighting (lean quorum, avoid global flaps), and
- canary-aware rollouts (allow gradual degradation windows for canaries).

Scope: prototype adapter and admission hook, integrate with existing readiness pipeline, add a simulation harness to validate SLO preservation under synthetic overloads and cross-region outage scenarios. Demo on canary service and one high-throughput frontend route.

Out-of-scope: changing kernel scheduling or deep runtime batching heuristics (those are separate RFCs).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Graded health score produced every 2s for prototype service and exposed via health API (0.0-1.0).
2) Admission hook uses score to implement three bands: accept, queue (soft shed), reject; documented thresholds configurable per-route.
3) Autoscaler consumes smoothed score to avoid scaling oscillations in our sim harness (reduce scale-up/scale-down events by >=40% vs baseline on synthetic 3x step traffic).
4) Multi-region failover tests: during a simulated region degradation, global SLO (99th latency for priority tokens) stays within target for remaining region with no cascading NotReady flips.
5) Confluence design + sequence diagram and runbook created; at least one engineering review sign-off.
6) End-to-end PR merged to staging and demo recorded; perf dashboard shows correct signal ingestion and label propagation to console.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff notes: aligned with SRE and Runtime teams. We agreed the adapter should be pluggable (config-driven feature flags) and initially scoped to runtime-facing frontends. Action: Marco to draft signal model.

2026-02-28 - Marco Ruiz: Posted signal model draft in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RUN/pages/Graded+Health+Adapter. Key signals: p50/p95/p99 latency, 1m/5m error rate, queue length normalized by worker capacity, token-weighted backlog. Seeking feedback from SRE by Mar 2.

2026-03-03 - Lina Gomez (SRE): Reviewed and suggested adding 'recent eviction rate' and 'kv-cache-miss-pressure' as signals. Concern: avoid heavy cardinality in metrics to keep ingestion cost low. Proposed smoothing kernel: exponential with 30s window.

2026-03-05 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented prototype scoring function and added sim harness scenarios. Initial sim shows reduced oscillations but an edge case where long-running canary requests cause score to dip and reject high-priority short requests. Proposed change: token-aware bucketing so short/high-priority requests are exempt from reject band when backlog is dominated by long tail jobs.

2026-03-09 - Design review (Emily Tran): Approved admission UX for console: three slider thresholds with per-route overrides. Asked to add telemetry labels for canary-id and token-tier to console tracebacks. Design doc: https://drive.redwood.com/design/graded-health-adapter-admission-ui.pdf

2026-03-12 - Marco Ruiz: Integrated autoscaler hysteresis hook. Running riot tests in staging: reduced scale flapping by ~52% on synthetic burst workloads (3 replicas flapping -> 1 stable scale-up). Captured logs and initial dashboard: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/health-adapter/staging. Opening PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4512
2026-03-13 - Aisha Patel: Note: Need runbook entries for manual override and emergency NotReady cutover. Also schedule cross-team demo with SRE and Console next week (Mar 18).
